title: Gauging Modulated Symmetries: Bond Algebras, Higher-Form Symmetries, and Symmetry-Enriched Topological Order
authors: Gustavo M. Yoshitome, Pedro R. S. Gomes, Guilherme Delfino
abstract: We develop a constructive framework for characterizing modulated symmetries and their gauging in $d$-dimensional lattice systems. The modulation profiles are organized as a finite-dimensional representation of the space group acting on a finite Abelian internal symmetry group. Since the corresponding automorphism group is finite, the nontrivial spatial action factors through a finite quotient of the space group, leading to periodic modulation patterns and providing a classification framework for discrete Abelian modulated symmetries. The symmetry-allowed local interactions are systematically obtained from a kernel construction, which also yields an algebra of open operators. Upon gauging, its elements are transmuted into extended Wilson and boundary operators while retaining their algebraic relations. In the deconfined regime, the resulting algebra realizes a mixed 't Hooft anomaly, providing a microscopic route to Abelian crystalline symmetry-enriched topological phases (SETs). These SETs do not mix electric and magnetic sectors, which transform in mutually contragredient representations, thereby preserving their braiding pairing. We illustrate the framework through explicit examples and show that several models present in the literature fit naturally within our construction.
summary: This work establishes a systematic mathematical framework to classify modulated symmetries in lattice models. By constructing the algebra of symmetry-allowed local interactions and performing a gauging procedure, the authors derive a direct microscopic understanding of Abelian crystalline symmetry-enriched topological phases. This provides powerful tools for predicting and characterizing exotic quantum states in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The paper develops a constructive framework to characterize modulated symmetries and their gauging in $d$-dimensional lattice systems.
main_result: This framework provides a microscopic route to Abelian crystalline symmetry-enriched topological (SET) phases, which are characterized by specific constraints on their electric and magnetic sectors.
method: The authors use a kernel construction to derive symmetry-allowed local interactions (the bond-algebra) and then analyze the gauging procedure to generate emergent higher-form quantum symmetries.
model_or_system: The study focuses on $d$-dimensional lattice systems possessing a space group symmetry and an internal discrete Abelian symmetry group. The analysis is systematic, linking the symmetry content to the structure of local interactions.
key_observables: Mixed 't Hooft anomaly, braiding pairing, topological entanglement entropy (implied by SETs).
important_parameters: The relationship $q + \chi = t$ links the number of symmetry generators ($q$), independent local interactions ($\chi$), and the stencil size ($t$).
main_assumptions: The space group action is assumed to factor through a finite quotient, leading to periodic modulation patterns.
figures_summary: TABLE I summarizes representative examples of modulated symmetries on 2D square lattices, listing parameters like $(q, \chi, t)$ and modulation periods.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the symmetry structure, deriving the constraints on local interactions via the bond-algebra, and then analyzing the consequences of gauging these symmetries to identify the resulting topological phases.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework for classifying topological phases based on underlying lattice symmetries is highly relevant for understanding exotic quantum states in strongly correlated materials.
